main_text.p: entia. Tam enim malos quàm bonos Principes esse à Deo constitutos, ipse alibi testatur Augustinus. [{a}Non tri-buamus dandi Regni & Imperij Potestatem, nisi soli Deo vero, qui dat felicitatem in Regno cœlorum solis pijs ; regnum verò terrenum, & pijs & impijs, sicut ei placet, cui nihil iniustè placet. Qui Mario Imperium dedit, ipse Caio Cæsari, qui Augusto, ipse & Neroni, qui Vespasianis vel Patri, vel Filio sua-uisimis Imperatoribus, ipse & Domi-tiano crudelissimo; & ne per singulos ire necesse sit, qui Constantino Christiano, ipse & Apostatæ Iuliano. Hæc omnia unus Deus & verus regit & gubernat, ut sibi placet, & si oc-Lib.5.de Ciuitat.Dei. cap.21. cultis causis, nunquid ideò iniu- stis ?]

page.notes: Marginal note a is printed beside the bracket and "Non". Left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Doubtful: "sua-uisimis" (the printed letters after the hyphen are read as "uisimis"). The top of the page is cut off, so the first paragraph is a fragment and is marked cont="true". The block of pale, mirrored text in the lower half of the column is show-through and was left out. The strip of hyphenated line ends at the far left belongs to the facing printed page and was left out. The handwritten pen mark at lower left was left out. The column to the right of the rule is blank.
